title: The Tamil King Who Burned His Enemy's Capital | Pallava Revenge at Vatapi #shorts

lines.text: In six forty two, a Pallava army marched far north, and is said to have burned an enemy capital.
lines.caps: in *642 | a *Pallava army | marched *north | and burned | an enemy *capital.

lines.text: The city was Vatapi. Today we call it Badami. And this was revenge.
lines.caps: the city | was *Vatapi | today | *Badami | this was | *revenge.

lines.text: Years earlier, the Chalukya king, Pulakeshin the second, had marched south, towards the Pallava capital, Kanchi.
lines.caps: years *earlier | the Chalukya king | *Pulakeshin | marched *south | towards *Kanchi.

lines.text: At Pullalur, near Kanchi, he met the Pallava king, Mahendravarman.
lines.caps: at *Pullalur | he met | the Pallava king | *Mahendravarman.

lines.text: Who won? Chalukya inscriptions claim a victory. Some historians read Pallava records the other way.
lines.caps: who *won? | Chalukya | *victory | Pallava records | the *other way.

lines.text: Most accounts agree Kanchi held. But northern lands were lost.
lines.caps: most accounts | Kanchi *held | but northern lands | were *lost.

lines.text: His son, Narasimhavarman, came to the throne around six thirty.
Around six forty two, he struck back. Accounts say he beat Pulakeshin near Kanchi, then marched on Vatapi.
lines.caps: around *642 | he *struck back | beat *Pulakeshin | then marched | on *Vatapi.

lines.text: Pulakeshin is believed to have died in the fighting. Vatapi was taken, and is said to have been burned.
lines.caps: Pulakeshin | *believed | to have *died | Vatapi | was *taken | and *burned.

lines.text: Narasimhavarman took a title: Vatapikonda, the one who took Vatapi.
lines.caps: a new *title | *Vatapikonda | the one | who *took Vatapi.

lines.text: Some accounts say the Pallavas held the city for about twelve years.
lines.caps: some accounts | held the city | about *twelve years.

lines.text: Tamil tradition names his general, Paranjothi, and says he later gave up war and became a saint.
lines.caps: Tamil *tradition | names *Paranjothi | he gave up *war | became a *saint.

lines.text: It also says he carried home a Ganesha statue, worshipped as Vatapi Ganapati. That is legend, not record.
lines.caps: a *Ganesha | statue | *Vatapi Ganapati | that is *legend | not *record.

lines.text: Today, Badami is known for its red sandstone caves. The fire is rarely told.
lines.caps: today | *Badami | red *sandstone caves | the *fire | is rarely *told.

lines.text: One defeat. One revenge. One burning city. Follow Aazhi for the stories behind the stories.
